title: AI call handling and missed-call booking for small electrical contractors

fixture.label: queue #11 benchmark case R3: a real idea from the product ideas register; the appetite is a test fixture

upstream_status.summary: Killed 2026-10-02 by its opportunity brief: Jobber Receptionist, Housecall Pro CSR AI and ServiceTitan AI Voice Agent bundle it; writing bookings into those suites is gated; plain AI receptionists cost $16.67-$49 (Beside, Rosie).

user: The owner, who misses calls while on a job
job: Answer and follow up on the calls the owner misses while working, and book the work.

evidence.claim: A trade-shop customer-service job posting ($20-24 an hour) lists following up on missed calls.
evidence.quote: Follow up on missed calls, open opportunities, and customers who may still need service

evidence.claim: A 1-star Housecall Pro App Store review says its AI answering acts like a robot pretending to be the owner.
evidence.quote: a robot pretending to be me, starts a conversation with my prospective customers then leaves em hanging if I don't jump in

evidence.claim: Housecall Pro's CSR AI answers calls and books jobs.
evidence.quote: answers every call, books the job, schedules the appointment, and provides a call log

evidence.claim: Jobber Receptionist is included in Jobber's Plus plan and an add-on for Grow.
evidence.quote: Jobber Receptionist is included with Plus plans and available as an add-on for Grow plans

evidence.claim: Rosie's AI receptionist costs $49 a month for solo owners.
evidence.quote: Professional $49 per month For solo owners and small businesses who can't always answer the phone.

open_unknowns.question: Would a shop pay for call booking outside the field-service suite it already uses?

appetite.note: Test fixture for the queue #11 benchmark: not the owner's appetite.

constraints.text: No contact with contractors or anyone else without the owner's go-ahead.
No real money (ads, deposits, paid tools) without the owner's rails and go-ahead.
